method: Every held-out record whose outcome was not exact, correctly unmatched or correctly abstained was inspected after the single holdout evaluation: its label and note, the decision's rule and signals, the OSM tags of every element involved, and the same record's decision under each declared ablation. Each is given the one cause that explains it. Nothing here changed the matcher, the policy or a label.

categories.curb_cut_onto_crossing: Matcher defect. A curb-cut piece lies along the end of the sidewalk and the start of the crossing way, or only the crossing. Class compatibility rates a crossing way 'different' from a sidewalk-family record, so the crossing is never claimed and the set is incomplete or wrong. The kerb node, where there is one, is still matched correctly.
categories.curb_cut_short_piece_carrier: Definition boundary. For a curb-cut piece of about a metre, whether it lies along a way is decided by two or three 1 m samples and the 45 degree alignment limit. The labeller cited only the kerb node, or a different stub, or was unsure whether the sidewalk belongs.
categories.diagonal_piece_at_untagged_junction: Matcher over-commits. A short piece lies diagonally (37-45 degrees) across an untagged junction of sidewalks and crossings with no kerb node within 2 m. The nearest sidewalk passes the 45 degree alignment limit and crossing ways are a different class, so nothing competes and the matcher names one sidewalk where the labeller could name none.
categories.corner_piece_between_chained_ways: Matcher over-commits. A corner piece lies between two ways that meet at the corner node. The topology rule treats ways sharing a node as one continuing facility, not competitors, so the matcher names the way claiming most of the piece where the labeller could not choose. With the topology rule off, all five abstain.
categories.stair_on_untagged_footway: Definition gap. OSM draws the walkway through the City's stair as a plain footway, not highway=steps. The labeller called the correspondence ambiguous because the stair is not tagged; the matcher matched the footway and leaves the missing steps tag to the attribute comparison, which reports the structure as Kitchener-only. The guide does not settle which reading is right, and one labeller took the matcher's reading on record 391945.
categories.structure_spans_more_than_osm_structure: Matcher defect. The City's structure record runs past the OSM structure onto its approaches, or across several short OSM pieces. The structure rule keeps only ways tagged as the structure, and the 5 m end slop drops structure pieces shorter than that, so the set is incomplete.
categories.end_slop_boundary: Threshold boundary. A few metres onto the next way beyond the 5 m end slop is counted as a second carrier; the labeller treated it as the junction.
categories.kerb_node_choice: Threshold boundary. Two kerb nodes lie within about 2 m of a corner piece. The matcher chooses by distance with a 0.5 m margin; the labeller chose by which crossing the piece serves, or could not choose.
categories.perpendicular_neighbour: Conservative abstention. A spur or stair with no OSM counterpart is touched at one end by a perpendicular path whose median distance is within 5 m, so the matcher abstains where the labeller saw nothing. Safe direction: no evidence is attached.
categories.osm_under_construction: Neither side matches. OSM has only a highway=construction way (a demolished bridge); the matcher does not treat construction as pedestrian and says no counterpart, the labeller called it ambiguous.
